posts.title: Can a verified microkernel actually secure a car?
posts.description: Can a verified microkernel actually secure a car? In July 2015, two security researchers took control of a Jeep Cherokee while a journalist was driving it on a St. Louis highway. They reached it over the cellular network, through the entertainment system. From there they got onto the vehicle's internal bus and started sending commands to things that steer and stop the car. posts.title: A history of microkernels
posts.description: A history of microkernels Most operating systems people use are monolithic. The kernel is a single large program running with full authority over the hardware, containing the scheduler, the memory manager, the file systems, the network stack, and the device drivers all in one address space.
